QA.Q: Which of the following is the main idea of the passage?
QA.passage:
Malala Yousafzai is widely admired for her courage and determination. Born in Pakistan in 1997, she grew up in a family that valued education. Her father, an educator, encouraged her to speak openly about the importance of schooling for girls. When Malala was still a child, she began writing about life under Taliban rule and about her wish to continue her education.

In 2012, Malala was attacked on her way home from school. She survived the attack and was taken to the United Kingdom for medical treatment. Instead of giving up, she continued to speak for girls who were denied access to education. Her recovery and determination attracted international attention.

In 2014, at the age of 17, Malala received the Nobel Peace Prize, becoming the youngest recipient at that time. Through the Malala Fund, she has continued to support education projects in different parts of the world. Her story shows that one person's courage can inspire millions and that difficulties do not have to define the end of a journey.
QA.B: Malala's courage and lifelong commitment to girls' education
QA.C: The history of education in the UK

QA.Q: What is the passage mainly about?
QA.passage:
A multicultural city is a place where people from different cultural backgrounds live, study and work together. Such cities can be exciting because residents can experience different languages, foods, festivals and traditions in everyday life. Children who grow up in multicultural communities may become more open-minded because they regularly meet people whose customs are different from their own.

However, cultural diversity does not automatically remove misunderstanding. People may have different ideas about personal space, communication styles, food, clothing or social behaviour. A gesture that is friendly in one culture may be interpreted differently in another. For this reason, successful multicultural communities need respect, patience and communication.

Schools can play an important role in building such communities. By organising cultural events, encouraging students to learn about different traditions and teaching them to question stereotypes, schools help young people develop cultural awareness. The goal is not to make everyone behave in the same way, but to help people understand differences and cooperate despite them.
QA.A: The disadvantages of living in cities
QA.B: The benefits and challenges of multicultural communities
